description: Desarrollamos HORIZON para el reto Navegante del sitio de alunizaje lunar. Creamos una plataforma 3D interactiva para evaluar la elevación solar, el relieve y las ventanas de enlace Direct-to-Earth en el polo sur lunar. Nuestro equipo abarca desarrollo web, análisis de datos y UI/UX. ¡Buscamos miembros con interés en física orbital, Three.js/WebGL o documentación técnica para consolidar una herramienta de misión de alto impacto.
summary:
Project HORIZON SPACE is a zero-latency, tactical survival-focused web application (PWA) designed to help mission planners evaluate landing sites at the lunar South Pole under scenarios involving launch delays.

At the Moon’s South Pole, low-angle sunlight and steep crater ridges create extreme shadows; a 48-hour launch delay can alter celestial alignments enough to block solar energy or sever direct communication links with Earth. Horizon Space addresses this through a split-screen interface that compares the nominal landing plan against delayed scenarios, controlled by a single time slider. By pre-computing 5-meter-resolution LOLA elevation models and NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides—mapped onto 15 km local terrain masks—our in-browser raycasting engine calculates solar and Earth-based occlusion in milliseconds.

This tool is vital because it transforms hours of complex orbital and topographical analysis into an immediate visual assessment of mission viability, helping to protect robotic landers and rovers from catastrophic losses of power or signal.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Project HORIZON SPACE is a zero-latency tactical Progressive Web App (PWA) for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. At the lunar South Pole, a 48-hour launch delay shifts celestial alignments enough for steep crater ridges to block low-angle sunlight or cut off Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communications. Horizon Space replaces hours of manual analysis with a 3-second visual verdict:

  • Split-Screen Comparison & Timeline: Compares the nominal landing plan (left) against a +24h/+48h delayed scenario (right) using a single interactive timeline slider, accounting for Earth-to-Moon transit profiles (7, 14, or 45 days).
  • Viability Advisor & Browser Raycasting: Pre-computes NASA LOLA 5m DEM topography (15 km radius) into a 720-direction horizon mask alongside 69,985 JPL Horizons ephemeris vectors (2026–2027). Our local raycasting engine detects terrain occlusion in under 12 ms, recommending optimal launch windows and triggering instant green (safe) or red (blackout/signal loss) alerts.

Impact & Tech Stack

  • Impact: Enables CLPS and Artemis planners to evaluate launch-delay risks in real time on any browser without backend servers, protecting robotic landers and rovers from power or signal loss.
  • Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Three Fiber, and Python (GDAL) for static JSON data preprocessing.
